final_message:
`buildPickList` is finished in `src/pickList.ts`. All 36 tests pass under `bun test`, and everything is committed. The types and the error class are unchanged.

**How it works:**
- **Reading the orders:** the whole text is read in one pass and every problem is noted. If there are any, the one highest up in the file is thrown as `OrderFormatError`.
- **Allocation:** stock is tracked in a separate list of remaining quantities, so the `stock` array and its lots are never changed. Each SKU's lots are tried earliest best-before first, undated lots last, ties by bin code. Priority orders go first, then the rest, each group in the order of the text.
- **Walking order:** picks are sorted aisle by aisle, alternating rack direction per aisle that actually has a pick, levels ascending. Picks at the same bin stay in the order they were allocated.

**Choices the spec left open:**
- **Empty orders and bad lines:** a malformed line doesn't count as an item. So in `ORDER 1001` / `OLIVE-500 x0` / `ORDER 1002`, the error is reported at line 1 (order 1001 has no items, and that is higher up). But in `ORDER 1001` / `OLIVE-500 x0` / `OLIVE-500 x1`, the order does have an item, so the error is at line 2. I first coded this wrongly (always line 1), and a test caught it.
- **Spacing:** I took "one or more spaces" literally. Only spaces are accepted between `ORDER`, the id and `!`, and between the SKU and `x<qty>`. Tabs are only stripped at the start and end of a line. `ORDER 10!` with no space is an error.
- **Repeated order ids:** a repeated id is an error even when the second one is marked as priority (`ORDER 1001 !` after `ORDER 1001`).

**Process:** I worked one test at a time and kept the test list in `TESTLIST.md`; all items are ticked. I committed after each passing step, but most commits also include the next test, which was still failing at that point. So some commits in the middle of the history don't pass `bun test` on their own; the last commit does.
